Abstract: Distinguishing visually similar characters is a persistent challenge for optical character recognition (OCR) systems, causing errors in critical applications of text digitization. abstract:

abstract:

authors: Karim Abdel Sadek, Federico Di Gennaro, Fanny Yang
abstract:

Abstract: Training models on their own outputs has attracted widespread attention as a possible route to advance AI capabilities. abstract:

abstract:

abstract:

Abstract: Preprocessing is an under-measured reliability risk in clinical prediction: a model can keep a similar AUROC and still change who receives an alert. abstract:

title: Ori: Drift-Aware Streaming $k$-PCA for Very Low-Rank LLM Training
authors: Xinyu Luo, Jincheng Zhou, Mengbo Wang, Zilin Shen, Nadia Atallah Lanman, Petros Drineas, Bruno Ribeiro, Brian Bullins
abstract:

Abstract: A prominent family of low-rank LLM optimizers, pioneered by GaLore, performs gradient-subspace projection: at each step, they project the gradient into a low-dimensional subspace and map the update back to the full model. authors: Pingchuan Ma, Rui Ding, Shuai Wang
abstract:

Abstract: LLM agents can now run causal discovery algorithms on a dataset and report what comes out. Abstract: In the age of data-driven decision-making, deep learning models have become powerful tools for uncovering patterns and making predictions that influence many aspects of society. title: On the tradeoff between robustness and geometric accuracy in adversarial training
authors: Rachel Morris, Ryan Murray, Kerrek Stinson
abstract:
arXiv:2610.22955v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: For non-parametric binary classification in the presence of an adversary, we prove an optimal quantitative estimate for adversarial classifiers controlling geometric accuracy, as measured by the Hausdorff distance to the Bayes classifier, in terms or their robustness, as encoded by the adversarial budget $\varepsilon$. This rigorously shows that robust classifiers sacrifice at most $O(\sqrt{\varepsilon})$ or $O(\varepsilon)$ in accuracy, depending on the regularity of the underlying Bayes classifier. Our results apply for adversaries determined by any norm on Euclidean space and in both the infinite and finite data settings.

abstract:

title: Where Prefill Expert Reduction Hurts MoE Models: A Few Prompt Tokens Carry Most of the Short-Answer F1 Loss
authors: Zhiyuan Wang
abstract:
arXiv:2610.22454v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Running prompt tokens through fewer routed experts during prefill is a simple way to make mixture-of-experts (MoE) serving cheaper, yet it is unclear what this damages. We locate the damage with token-, layer- and attention-path interventions on short-answer question answering in four MoE families. At half the experts the F1 loss of three families is mostly answer form: the model still finds the answer but stops answering briefly. authors: Paulo Pintor, Rog\'erio Costa, Jos\'e Moreira
abstract:

Abstract: Runtime query similarity identification supports several activities, including workload analysis, identifying recurring behaviour, auditing, debugging, and anomaly detection. Existing methods for evaluating query similarity mostly rely on SQL text, execution plans, or result values but do not account for input data or how results are derived during query execution.
  This paper proposes a novel approach using data provenance for query-template identification. We construct query-level profiles that capture explicit data dependencies, occurrence frequencies, and structural properties by aggregating tuple-level Lineage and Why-provenance across entire query results. We also derive Provenance Structural Descriptors (PSD), which summarise these profiles using a small set of numerical features.

title: Reading the News Without Hindsight: NoLBERT Topics and the Cross-Section of Stock Returns
authors: Kevin Foley, Jonathan Hartadi, Shivesh Prakash, Charishma Takkallapalli, Swapnil Vatsal
abstract:
arXiv:2610.22745v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Language models that read financial news are usually trained on text from the same years used to test them, so a backtest can reward hindsight. We build news topics from NoLBERT, an encoder pretrained only on text published between 1976 and 1995, adapted into a sentence encoder by contrastive fine-tuning on passages of the same article, with no labels or returns. We compare it with LDA, MiniLM and FinBERT readers on 1.26 million articles from 2012 to 2024, convert each reader's topics into attention shocks and stock exposures, and forecast the returns of the 1,000 largest US stocks with eight models at three rebalancing frequencies. title: ToPA: Block-wise Toeplitz Adaptation for Expressive and Efficient Fine-Tuning
authors: Sicong Li, Qianqian Xu, Zhiyong Yang, Zitai Wang, Longtao Huang, Xiaochun Cao, Qingming Huang
abstract:

Abstract: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) has emerged as a prevalent strategy for adapting large pre-trained models. Among PEFT techniques, reparameterization-based methods, particularly those that employ low-rank or sparsity structures, have attracted significant attention. However, these approaches often underperform full fine-tuning. Specifically, low-rank methods constrain the update rank, which is misaligned with the inherently high-rank nature of full fine-tuning. In contrast, sparsity-based techniques limit the flexibility of the parameter space and compromise connectivity across weights. To overcome these limitations, we explore the use of Toeplitz matrices, whose entries are constant along each diagonal, therefore providing a compact parameterization without imposing explicit rank or sparsity constraints. title: Competence-Based Evaluation of Logical Reasoning in Large Language Models
authors: Jize Jiang, Chengxiang Zhai
abstract:
arXiv:2610.22894v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have brought impressive performance across diverse tasks; however, shortcomings remain in logical reasoning, including inconsistencies under linguistic variation. To improve the reasoning capacity of LLMs, we must be able to accurately measure their reasoning capacity. Current benchmarks primarily report single accuracy numbers on selected reasoning tasks. Such a performance-based evaluation methodology says little about a model's generalization capacity in reasoning. To address this limitation, we argue for a different evaluation paradigm, called competence-based evaluation (CBE), which tests whether models reliably apply the same competence across a family of problems. A parameterized generator scales complexity while keeping the required competence fixed, and matched answer-preserving presentations test correctness beyond one formulation. title: What Shapes Brain Alignment of Large Language Models during Dialogue? Insights from Language Production and Comprehension
authors: Yuko Nakagi, Yuya Chiba, Yasue Kishino
abstract:
arXiv:2610.22961v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Brain alignment of large language models (LLMs) offers a way to investigate representational similarities between LLMs and the human brain during language processing. While previous studies have mainly focused on passive language comprehension, little is known about such alignment during dialogue, in which speakers engage in both language production and comprehension. In this study, using fMRI data collected during dialogue, we examine brain alignment during language production and comprehension across LLM layers and brain regions. We assess its association with the intrinsic dimension (ID) of LLM representations and the contributions of several interpretable linguistic and communicative features. Our results reveal distinct patterns of brain alignment between production and comprehension, as well as strong associations with ID in brain regions associated with each processing mode. title: DIFFLET: A Fast Inference Engine for Diffusion Transformer Models on AWS Trainium
authors: Bin Ma, Min Yu, Vijay Kodamalla, Jialin Liu, Dong Li
abstract:
arXiv:2610.23047v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: On AWS Trainium2, every component of a diffusion model runs as a program compiled ahead of time for fixed shapes, while pipelines differ across models, prompt lengths across requests, and caching decisions across denoising steps. We present Difflet, a serving engine in which five model pipelines share one compilation backend, joint attention is split across cores by attention head, and a host controller decides at each denoising step whether to run the denoiser or reuse its earlier output. A small probe program computes the caching signal on the device and returns one number per step, and a resident model process keeps every program loaded across requests. Across five image and video model families, fused attention accelerates denoiser steps by 1.2-4.3x over the same framework using PyTorch/XLA attention, and at 32.8k visual tokens it is the only attention that compiles. title: Learning angles for quantum approximate optimization
authors: Johannes Jakubik, Isabelle Wittmann, Zaheed Gaffoor, Gciniwe Simphiwe Baloyi, Craig Mahlasi, Etienne Vos, Thomas Brunschwiler, Daniel J. Egger
abstract:

Abstract: The Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) and its variants are leading algorithms to help solve challenging combinatorial optimization problems. QAOA maps these problems to Ising Hamiltonians such that their ground state is the desired solution. Candidate solutions are then drawn from a variational quantum circuit. The performance of QAOA hinges on a set of variational angles. However, finding good angles is an instance-specific and computationally expensive non-convex classical optimization task. Here, we learn the mapping from the problem instance to high-quality QAOA angles. Our learned models replace the per-instance optimization, that we call the solver, with a single forward pass that is several orders of magnitude faster than the solver with a near identical quality. Abstract: Isogai's case A, a pitch-plunge aerofoil whose elastic axis lies half a chord ahead of the leading edge, has a folded transonic flutter boundary in inviscid flow: near the bottom of the transonic dip several flutter speeds coexist at one Mach number. title: The Loss or the Architecture? What Matters in Survival Analysis with Competing Risks
authors: Julie Alberge, Ga\"el Varoquaux, Judith Ab\'ecassis
abstract:

Abstract: Often, \emph{eg} in healthcare and predictive maintenance, what matters is which of several competing causes will strike first, and with what probability: survival analysis with competing risks. Corresponding deep learning methods are developed as bundles: a new architecture together with a new training loss, tested on one to five datasets against a handful of baselines. Thus, a state-of-the-art result cannot be attributed to the architecture, the loss, or the evaluation protocol. We vary the two axes independently, three losses, two of them strictly proper, on four backbones, across two modalities that tease the axes apart: 20 tabular and 3 pathology-image datasets. title: HydraLLM: Adaptive Width Slicing for Elastic Text and Vision-Language Models
authors: Oscar Kemme, Janek Haberer, Ali Hojjat, Olaf Landsiedel
abstract:
arXiv:2610.23455v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: LLMs and LVLMs are increasingly deployed across heterogeneous hardware, ranging from data-center GPUs to resource-constrained edge devices. Their fixed-size architectures limit the ability to reuse a single model across deployment settings with different compute, latency, and model-size targets. We introduce HydraLLM, an elastic MQA-based architecture. Its number of active attention heads determines the effective widths of the embeddings, attention projections, feed-forward layers, and the output head, forming a nested family of subnetworks within a single parameter set. We introduce a static-to-elastic conversion pipeline that, starting from a pre-trained model checkpoint, includes importance-driven weight reordering and stochastic subnetwork training with knowledge distillation. title: Graphlet-based Decentralized Finance Transaction Method Classification
authors: C\'{e}lestin Coquid\'{e}, Alessio Brini, Natkamon Tovanich
abstract:
arXiv:2610.23466v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Decentralized Finance (DeFi) transactions involve complex interactions among accounts, smart contracts, and tokens. We investigate whether network topology can identify transaction methods that describe DeFi operations. We extract directed graphlet features to classify the 30 most frequent methods. Our results show that graphlet features complement event log counts in improving classification performance. Using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), we further derive model explanations that reveal method-specific graphlet structural patterns.

title: Towards optimal selection schedules for online active learning
authors: Hugo Cui, Francesca Mignacco, Francesco Mori
abstract:

Abstract: We consider the problem of online linear classification, where a stream of unlabeled samples is available, and annotation is costly. We focus on the realizable case, under Gaussian design, in the high-dimensional regime where data dimension and number of unlabeled samples grow proportionally. We consider two objectives: 1) the generalization error under a labeling budget, and 2) a cumulative cost function where mistakes have unit cost and queries cost $\Delta$. authors: Mohamed Mallat, Michele Panariello, Massimiliano Todisco, Nicholas Evans, Anthony Larcher

Abstract: Self-supervised speech models such as WavLM achieve strong spoofing detection performance, yet which layers encode the most spoof-relevant information and what acoustic properties they capture remain opaque. title: Bridging the Language Gap in Scholarly Data II: Enhancing Gender Inference for Chinese Names
authors: Lisette Esp\'in-Noboa, Mingrong She, Ana Maria Jaramillo, Liuhuaying Yang
abstract:
arXiv:2610.23734v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Perceived gender inference from names is important for inclusive scientometrics research, yet existing methods perform poorly on non-Western scholars. We address this gap for Chinese names, which appear in two forms, Hanzi and Pinyin, its Romanized form (e.g., Zhang Wei, Li Na). In international bibliographic records, names are often available only in Pinyin. However, a single pinyin name can correspond to multiple distinct hanzi characters with different gender associations, so gender inference from Pinyin alone is intrinsically ambiguous. To address this, we first develop two hanzi models, a regression model that produces a continuous gender score from 0 (male) to 1 (female), and a classification model that outputs one of three labels (\em{male}, \em{neutral}, \em{female}). title: Task-aligned spectral inductive biases in parameterized quantum circuits
authors: Felix Frohnert, Adri\'an P\'erez-Salinas, Sebastian Lange, Marcus Schwaebisch, Evert van Nieuwenburg, Vedran Dunjko
abstract:

Abstract: Parameterized quantum circuits are widely investigated in quantum machine learning, yet how their architecture can provide task-aligned inductive biases remains poorly understood. We study data reuploading quantum circuits with two distinct inputs: a signal that varies between samples and a fixed, task-defined spectral query that specifies how the signal should be probed. We show that encoding the query can change the circuit's hypothesis class over the signal by modulating how its existing signal frequencies are combined, without introducing new sample-dependent information. This mechanism matches tasks built on nonuniform Fourier transforms, whose evaluation frequencies specify the query and whose sampling positions guide its encoding. abstract:

Abstract: Poisson non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) is a widely used method to find interpretable "parts-based" decompositions of count data. While many variants of Poisson NMF exist, existing methods assume that the "parts" in the decomposition combine additively. This assumption may be natural in some settings, but not in others. Here we introduce Poisson NMF with the shifted-log link function to relax this assumption. The shifted-log link function has a single tuning parameter, and as this parameter varies the model changes from assuming that parts combine additively (i.e., standard Poisson NMF) to assuming that parts combine more multiplicatively. abstract:

Abstract: We present Mesh Field Theory (MeshFT) and its neural realization, MeshFT-Net: a structure-preserving framework for mesh-based continuum physics that cleanly separates the physics' topological structure from its metric structure. authors: Donghoon Han, Minseop Jung, Dong Woo Kwak, SeungJae Lee, Junhoo Lee
abstract:

Abstract: Conditional memory expands language-model capacity through selective lookup, but the full embedding table must remain available for every possible input. abstract:

Abstract: Vision Transformers (ViTs) have demonstrated strong performance in many computer vision tasks but do not naturally extend beyond the natural image domain. One important example is Fourier-space data, which is used to represent a rich and diverse set of modalities, including medical imaging and microscopy. arXiv:2610.32452v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Developing multiple instance learning pipelines for the classification of whole-slide images involves many interdependent design decisions and expertise in both pathology and machine learning. We present AutoMIL, an open-source framework that applies principles from the field of automated machine learning to tackle this task by automating integral pipeline steps, such as preprocessing, training and evaluation. In a benchmark evaluation with default settings, AutoMIL reached ROC-AUC scores of 0.94 on UBC-OCEAN, 0.99 on PCam and 0.93-0.96 on a TCGA-NSCLC subset, comparable to specialised pipelines in related work. Ensembling mainly improved performance on imbalanced data, showing that an automated pipeline must adapt to dataset characteristics. AutoMIL thus provides an accessible baseline for whole-slide image classification without manual pipeline configuration.

title: PathJev: Decision-Native Vision-Language Modelling for Histopathology
authors: Cristian Tommasino, Antonio M. Rinaldi
abstract:
arXiv:2610.32478v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Vision-language models used for decisions in histopathology rarely return calibrated probabilities over the candidates a user cares about. Decision-native models write a question and a candidate set chosen at run time into the input and return a normalised distribution from a small decision head in one forward pass. We build PathJev-P, a decision-native model for histopathology: MedGemma-1.5-4B with LoRA adapters and a decision head, trained on 40,000 patch states from three public collections whose expert labels are turned into typed questions with organ-specific candidate sets and a "none of these" option. Abstract: Photonic crystal fibers (PCFs) underpin critical applications in telecommunications, sensing, and high-power laser delivery, yet their design remains a manual, expert-intensive process that couples geometric intuition with deep waveguide physics. Vision-language models (VLMs) offer a promising path toward automating PCF design, but can they truly reason about photonic physics from microscopy images, or do they merely recognize visual patterns? abstract:

Abstract: Ki67 is a key marker of tumor proliferation in breast cancer, but its quantification from immunohistochemistry images normally depends on supervised classifiers trained per dataset. We examine the role of frozen pretrained visual representations in annotation-free Ki67 cell typing. To this end, we use K-CLUE, a framework that segments individual nuclei, represents each nucleus with a pretrained encoder, reduces the resulting embeddings with principal component analysis, and separates Ki67-positive from Ki67-negative nuclei using k-means clustering, without task-specific training or manual annotations. title: Augmentation Strategy for DINO in Glaucoma Classification
authors: Ashish Kumar Meena, Chandra Sekhar Seelamantula
abstract:
arXiv:2610.32511v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Self-supervised learning (SSL) offers a promising approach to medical image representation learning, yet augmentation strategies of SSL frameworks validated on natural images do not reliably transfer to specialized medical imaging domains. We analyze DINO, a knowledge-distillation based SSL framework, and empirically demonstrate that its default augmentation strategy produces unreliable representations for retinal fundus images, degrading downstream glaucoma classification performance. Guided by the principle that effective cropped views should share minimal redundant information while retaining clinically relevant signal, we redesign DINO's augmentation strategy. title: Fast and Useful: Adapting Distilled Generators for Visual Learning
authors: Patryk Bartkowiak, Dominik Michels, S\"oren Pirk, Wojciech Pa{\l}ubicki
abstract:

Abstract: Distilled text-to-image models generate images quickly, but classifiers trained on those images can perform substantially worse than classifiers trained on images from their slower base models. We adapt released distilled generators to produce better training data while retaining fast generation. We fit a low-rank update to the student's first prediction so that it reaches an intermediate state produced by its unguided base, then disable the update and let the unchanged student finish generation. The base supplies training targets and is absent at inference. Guided targets and shorter jumps give classifiers lower accuracy in our ablations, showing why the state used for supervision matters. Across three generator families, the adapted images train better classifiers than images from the released students. Abstract: Geospatial foundation models (GeoFMs) are costly to pretrain, yet model families often repeat this process across backbone scales and sensing modalities. Abstract: Camera-trap species classification is dominated by large models from well-resourced organisations, which often lack the species-level distinctions regional conservation needs, such as native red versus invasive grey squirrels in the UK. title: Hair Segmentation and Skin Characterization on Macroscopic Dermatological Images for Laser Treatment Parameterization
authors: Alex Navarro Navarro, Marc Arriaga Hidalgo, Carlos Moreno Rubio, Maxime Talarmain, Noelia Vaquero Gallardo
abstract:

Abstract: Current light-based devices, such as laser hair removal, intense pulsed light (IPL), vascular laser therapy, and dermatologic phototherapy, are widely used in clinical dermatology but rely heavily on subjective manual parameterization or uncalibrated point-based colorimeters. To overcome these limitations, this work presents a unified system for hair segmentation and skin characterization in macroscopic dermatological images. Unlike most existing literature that relies on dermoscopic datasets captured under highly controlled conditions, our approach is specifically designed for macroscopic images that replicate real clinical laser treatments. title: DriveOSS: Dataset and Benchmark for 3D Anomaly Segmentation and Open-set Semantic Segmentation in Autonomous Driving
authors: Zhiran Yan, Savankumar Bhanderi, Sourabh Lolge, Rui Song, Girdharbhai Paneliya, Shiva Agrawal, Gordon Elger

Abstract: Recent advances in 3D semantic segmentation have significantly improved scene understanding in autonomous driving. However, existing methods are typically developed under a closed-set assumption and evaluated under standard driving conditions, where all categories are known in advance. In real-world driving, autonomous vehicles inevitably encounter previously unseen objects, making closed-set perception insufficient for safe deployment. title: Cross-Architectural Feature Fusion for Coronary Artery Stenosis Detection in X-ray Angiography
authors: Haobo Zhu, Mojtaba Lashgari, Jason Chai, Giovanni Luigi De Maria, Vicente Grau, Abhirup Banerjee
abstract:

Abstract: Coronary artery disease remains a leading cause of mortality, with stenosis detection from invasive X-ray Coronary Angiography (XCA) critical for diagnosis. title: Consomm\'e: Conditioned Token Merging for Split Inference
authors: Man Ngo, Jan S. Rellermeyer
abstract:
arXiv:2610.32794v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Split inference partitions a Vision Transformer between a resource-constrained edge device and a server. However, transmitting intermediate tokens across the communication channel is costly. Deploying fine-tuned backbones to every endpoint becomes expensive as well. We study token reduction for split inference under a frozen backbone, where only a small adapter is shipped. We observe that the CLS token plays a dual role: it acts as the global summary the receiver needs for classification, and it serves as a signal on which patches to keep. We propose Consomm\'e, a method utilizing both characteristics. There, an information bottleneck compresses the CLS token into a compact latent which is transmitted in place of the full CLS token and conditions a learned patch gate merging patches into exactly $k$ tokens via soft assignment. title: SPOOK: Sparse Pixel Optimization for Off-Manifold Knowledge in Vision Encoders
authors: Ankit Gupta, Akshat Pandya, Christoph Adami, Emily Dolson
abstract:

Abstract: Modern vision encoders are widely used as semantic representations, but the relationship between embedding similarity and human-visible semantics can become unclear far from the natural-image manifold. authors: Tarunya Prasad, Bharatesh Chakravarthi
abstract:

Abstract: Semantic misinformation can arise when an authentic image is paired with a caption that changes or distorts its narrative. Because the image itself may contain no visible signs of manipulation, methods designed to detect pixel-level artifacts can miss these misleading image-caption pairs. Abstract: Raman spectroscopy generates large volumes of unlabeled data that are difficult to exploit with conventional supervised learning. authors: Sachin Konan, Jonathan Liu, Zhuang Liu
abstract:

Abstract: Automated research is largely evaluated by benchmark performance, but the value of research rarely reduces to a single score. However, what if, given only the paper, we could predict its peer-review decision directly? Abstract: Combined optoacoustic (OptA) and ultrasound imaging is a promising modality across a wide range of pathologies. Current methods rely mostly on visual data, while acoustic sensing has shown potential to provide complementary information on surgical activity. First approaches for the localisation of surgical activity relied on microphone arrays and acoustic beamforming. title: Closing the Modality Gap via Simplex-Constrained Representations
authors: Shubham Gupta, Siva Reddy, Perouz Taslakian, Valentina Zantedeschi, Cem Subakan
abstract:
arXiv:2610.32890v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: While multimodal contrastive models like CLIP and CLAP successfully learn shared representations, their embeddings typically exhibit a persistent \emph{modality gap}. We propose addressing this separation through a purely geometric approach: changing the embedding domain from the unit sphere, $S^{d-1}$, to the probability simplex, $\Delta^{d-1}$. Although both manifolds share the same intrinsic dimension, the simplex acts as a structural prior; its nonnegative, unit-mass constraints serve as a cross-modal calibration that forces both modalities to ground themselves in the same coordinate system. By attaching lightweight softmax adapters and using Total Variation similarity, we reduce the centroid $\ell_2$ gap by 97--99\% across five multimodal retrieval benchmarks. This confirms that simplicial geometry induces genuine semantic alignment, matching or exceeding the retrieval performance of standard unconstrained models.

authors: Teng Xu, Taotao Zhou, Youjia Wang, Peng Yang, Simin Tang, Kuixiang Shao, Zifeng Tang, Yifei Liu, Xinyuan Chen, Yihan Liu, Zhengning Xu, Boyang Xia, Hongshuang Wang, Xiaohui Wang, Huoqing Luo, Jingya Wang, Ji Hu, Jingyi Yu

abstract:

title: Half-Truths Break Similarity-Based Retrieval
authors: Bora Kargi, Arnas Uselis, Seong Joon Oh
abstract:
arXiv:2602.23906v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: When a text description is extended with an additional detail, image-text similarity should drop if that detail is wrong. authors: Nermin Samet, Gilles Puy, Renaud Marlet
abstract:
arXiv:2604.01361v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: This paper presents a new method for the zero-shot open-vocabulary semantic segmentation (OVSS) of 3D automotive lidar data. To circumvent the recognized image-text modality gap that is intrinsic to approaches based on Vision Language Models (VLMs) such as CLIP, our method relies instead on image generation from text, to create prototype images. title: Order Matters: Competition-Guided Query Ordering for RNN-Based Object Detection
authors: Shengjian Wu, Li Sun, Yu Shangguan, Qingli Li
abstract:

title: MINER: Modeling Inter- and Intra-Person Variance for Reidentification
authors: Oron Nir, Eliyahu Strugo, Ariel Shamir
abstract:
arXiv:2610.28941v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Clothes-Changing Person Re-Identification (CC-ReID) remains challenging due to drastic appearance shifts across outfits. Most prior works devise biometric signal-extraction heuristics to enhance inter-person variance, e.g., using segmentation masks, while leaving intra-person variance uncontrolled. We present MINER, a simple model-agnostic framework that suppresses garment bias by contrasting hard examples and adaptively balancing dataset-dependent intra- and inter-person variance. Extensive experiments show that MINER improves retrieval across CC-ReID benchmarks, achieving state-of-the-art performance on four datasets and ranking among the leaders in all three tracks of the open TVRID RGB-Depth ReID challenge.

abstract:

Abstract: Robot foundation models are typically evaluated through costly closed-loop rollouts, motivating low-cost offline proxies for model capability. Abstract: Full-waveform inversion (FWI) reconstructs sound-speed fields from measured waveforms, by solving an optimization problem that minimizes the discrepancy between measured waveforms and those predicted by a numerical wave-propagation model.
